prompt: Write a note to a friend about a neighbor's advice about your garden. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the note only.
final_message:
Hi Maren,

You'll laugh when I tell you what happened over the fence on Saturday. I was crouched in the tomato bed, glaring at the yellowing leaves, when Mr. Alvarez from next door wandered over with his coffee and said, "You're loving them to death."

Apparently, that's my problem. He watched me water every evening for weeks, a little sprinkle on top, and he says that's the worst thing I could do. His advice: water deeply, but only two or three times a week, right at the base of the plant, and in the early morning so the leaves dry out fast. Shallow daily watering, he says, teaches the roots to stay near the surface and invites every fungus in the county to move in. I felt a bit called out, but he was kind about it.

He also told me to stop crowding the bed. I'd packed the seedlings in about a foot apart because I couldn't bear to waste space. He thinks they need closer to two feet so air can move through. Then he pointed at the lower leaves and said to pinch off anything touching the soil. I did it right then, and it felt strange, like I was hurting them, but the plants look tidier already.

The best tip was about the basil. He said to plant it right beside the tomatoes. His wife has done it for thirty years, and he swears it keeps the bugs down and makes the tomatoes taste better. I have no idea whether the science backs that up, but I had a flat of basil sitting on the porch anyway, so I tucked some in. If nothing else, we'll have caprese all August.

Then he disappeared into his garage and came back with a bucket of crushed eggshells and a handful of coffee grounds. "For calcium," he said, "and don't ask me to explain it." I think he's right about the blossom end rot, though, because that's exactly what happened to my first few fruits last summer.

I'll admit I was skeptical, since I've been gardening on my own for years and he's only lived there since spring. But he's grown more tomatoes than I've had hot dinners, and his yard looks like a magazine spread. I'm going to follow all of it and see what happens.

Come by in a few weeks and judge for yourself. I'll save you a tomato, and maybe a bit of basil too.

Love,
[name]
